topics.title: Present simple and continuous
topics.brief: State vs action verbs; present continuous for temporary situations, annoyance (always) and arrangements; present simple for timetables.

topics.title: Present perfect simple and continuous
topics.brief: for/since/just/yet/already/still; unfinished time; result vs activity; how long vs how many; with superlatives and first time.

topics.title: Narrative tenses
topics.brief: Past simple, past continuous, past perfect simple and continuous together in a story; sequencing; when/while/as; by the time.

topics.title: used to, would, be used to, get used to
topics.brief: Past habits and states vs present habits; be/get used to + -ing; would only for repeated actions.

topics.title: Future forms
topics.brief: will/going to/present continuous/present simple; future continuous and future perfect; be about to, be likely to; time clauses (when/as soon as + present).

topics.title: Obligation, permission and advice
topics.brief: must/have to/should/ought to/needn't/don't have to/mustn't; be allowed to; had better; past forms (had to, should have).

topics.title: Speculation and deduction
topics.brief: must/might/may/could/can't for present and past (+ have + participle); degrees of certainty; continuous forms (must be joking).

topics.title: Conditionals: zero to third
topics.brief: The four types with their meanings; unless/as long as/provided that/in case/even if; were in the second conditional; alternatives to will in results.

topics.title: Mixed conditionals
topics.brief: Past cause with present result and present state with past result.

topics.title: wish, if only, would rather, it's time
topics.brief: wish/if only + past, past perfect and would; would rather + past; it's (high) time + past; as if/as though.

topics.title: The passive in all tenses
topics.brief: Forms across tenses and with modals; by + agent; verbs with two objects; it is said that / he is said to; when to prefer the passive.

topics.title: Causative: have/get something done
topics.brief: have/get + object + participle in all tenses; get sb to do; have sb do; make/let/allow; have something happen to you.

topics.title: Reported speech
topics.brief: Tense, pronoun, time and place shifts; reported questions (if/whether, word order); commands and requests; when the tense does not change.

topics.title: Reporting verbs and their patterns
topics.brief: suggest/recommend + -ing; deny/admit + -ing; accuse sb of; insist on; warn/advise/persuade sb (not) to; agree/offer/refuse + to; apologise for.

topics.title: Relative clauses
topics.brief: Defining vs non-defining (commas, that, omission); whose/where/when/why; which referring to a whole clause; prepositions in relative clauses; reduced relatives (-ing/-ed).

topics.title: Verb patterns: gerund and infinitive
topics.brief: Verbs + -ing vs + to; verbs that change meaning (remember/forget/stop/try/regret/mean/go on); adjectives + to; prepositions + -ing; make/let + bare infinitive.

topics.title: Contrast and concession
topics.brief: although/even though/though; despite/in spite of (+ -ing/the fact that); whereas/while; however/nevertheless/on the other hand; position and punctuation.

topics.title: Purpose, reason and result
topics.brief: so that/in order to/so as to/to; because of/due to/owing to/as/since; so…that/such…that; too/enough; as a result/therefore/consequently.

topics.title: Comparison
topics.brief: Comparatives and superlatives (regular and irregular); modifiers (far/much/a lot/slightly/by far/easily); as…as / not as…as / twice as…as; the + comparative, the + comparative; like vs as.

topics.title: Articles and quantifiers
topics.brief: a/an/the/zero article with general, specific and abstract nouns; countable/uncountable; few/a few/little/a little; plenty of/hardly any; all/both/neither/either/each/every/none of.

topics.title: Adjectives and adverbs
topics.brief: Order of adjectives; -ed vs -ing; gradable and ungradable adjectives with intensifiers (very/absolutely/really); adverb position (frequency, manner, sentence adverbs); adjectives vs adverbs (hard/hardly, late/lately).

topics.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences and basic inversion
topics.brief: What I need is…; It was Sofia who…; The reason (why)…is; Not only…but also; Never/Rarely + inversion (introductory); so/neither/nor do I.

topics.title: Questions: indirect, tags and echo
topics.brief: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where…); question tags with all auxiliaries, imperatives (will you?), let's (shall we?); negative questions; echo questions and short answers.

topics.title: Word formation for Use of English Part 3
topics.brief: Noun/verb/adjective/adverb families; negative prefixes (un/in/im/il/ir/dis/mis); suffixes (-ness/-ment/-tion/-ity/-ful/-less/-able/-ive/-ly); compound adjectives; plural or negative? — reading the sentence for the right form.

topics.title: The perfect aspect across tenses
topics.brief: Present, past and future perfect, simple and continuous; by/by the time/before; perfect infinitive and perfect -ing; subtle differences (has lived vs has been living).

topics.title: Advanced narrative and the future in the past
topics.brief: Past perfect continuous; was going to / would / was to (have) for plans that changed; would for past habits vs refusal; historic present for drama.

topics.title: Advanced ways of talking about the future
topics.brief: be to / be about to / be due to / be bound to / be on the verge of; future continuous for politeness and assumptions; future perfect continuous; will for assumptions and habits; shall in formal contexts.

topics.title: Unreal past and hypothetical meaning
topics.brief: as if/as though (+ past/past perfect); would rather/sooner (+ past for other subjects); it's (high/about) time; suppose/supposing/what if; wish + would for irritation; if only with all three times.

topics.title: Modal verbs: fine distinctions
topics.brief: needn't have vs didn't need to; may/might as well; could have (missed opportunity/annoyance); should/ought to have; will/would for habits and assumptions; dare and need as modals; be supposed to.

topics.title: Speculating about the past
topics.brief: must/can't/couldn't/may/might + have + participle; continuous forms (must have been waiting); was/were to have; ought to have; hedged speculation in formal writing.

topics.title: Advanced conditionals
topics.brief: Inverted conditionals (Had I known / Should you require / Were it not for); but for / if it weren't for; if + were to / if + should; provided that / on condition that / whether or not / assuming that; implied conditions (otherwise, or else).

topics.title: Inversion after negative and limiting adverbials
topics.brief: never/rarely/seldom/little/nowhere; not until/not only/no sooner…than/hardly…when/scarcely; only then/only when/only by; under no circumstances/on no account/in no way; so + adjective…that / such…that; inversion after as and than.

topics.title: Cleft sentences
topics.brief: it-clefts (It was the message that mattered), wh-clefts (What matters is…), all/the only thing…, the reason/place/person…, reversed wh-clefts (That's what I meant); clefts for contrast and correction.

topics.title: Emphasis and fronting
topics.brief: Emphatic do/does/did; fronting objects and adverbials (This I can accept); intensifying adverbs (utterly, downright, thoroughly) and collocation; own and very; the thing is; emphatic whatever/whoever.

topics.title: Advanced passive structures
topics.brief: Impersonal passive (it is believed that / she is believed to have); get-passive; passive infinitives and gerunds (to be told / being told); need + -ing; have/get something done vs have something happen; passive with phrasal verbs.

topics.title: Reporting: verbs, patterns and distance
topics.brief: Reporting verbs with their patterns (deny/insist/urge/object to/threaten/accuse of/blame for/dissuade from); reporting with hedges (claim/allege/is said to/is thought to); reported questions and requests; reporting without backshift; summarising what was said.

topics.title: Advanced verb patterns
topics.brief: Verbs + object + infinitive/-ing (I saw him leave / leaving); perfect and continuous infinitives (seems to have been); passive infinitives; verb + preposition + -ing; can't help/bear/stand; to vs to + -ing after object to/look forward to/be used to.

topics.title: Participle clauses
topics.brief: Present, past and perfect participle clauses (Having finished…, Built in 1900…); reduced relatives; with + noun + participle; participles after conjunctions (when asked, if given); avoiding dangling participles.

topics.title: Advanced relative clauses
topics.brief: Preposition + whom/which; whereby/wherein; whatever/whichever/whoever; of which/whose with things; all of whom / some of which; non-finite relatives (the first person to…); which for whole clauses in formal writing.

topics.title: Nominalisation and academic style
topics.brief: Turning verbs and adjectives into nouns (fail → failure, likely → likelihood); noun phrases with pre- and post-modification; abstract nouns with the + noun + of; impersonal subjects; when NOT to nominalise.

topics.title: Hedging and impersonal structures
topics.brief: it seems/appears/would seem that; tend to; arguably/presumably/apparently; there is some evidence that; modals for tentativeness (may/might/could); one; passive to avoid naming the agent; softeners in speech (sort of, I'd say).

topics.title: Discourse markers and cohesion
topics.brief: Formal linkers (albeit, notwithstanding, hence, thereby, whereby, in that); sequencing and referencing (the former/the latter, the above, such); spoken markers (mind you, as I was saying, anyway, that said); cohesion through repetition and synonyms.

topics.title: Substitution and ellipsis
topics.brief: so/not after think/hope/suppose; do so/did so; one/ones; ellipsis after auxiliaries and to (I'd like to); if so / if not; omitting repeated subjects and verbs; the same; leaving out that and relative pronouns.

topics.title: Concession and contrast at C1
topics.brief: much as / however + adjective / no matter how / whatever; whilst; albeit; even so / all the same / that said; granted / admittedly; for all + noun; may…but; as in Tired as he was.

topics.title: Advanced comparison
topics.brief: the + comparative, the + comparative with ellipsis; nowhere near / nothing like / by far / every bit as / just as; not so much X as Y; comparatives with clauses (than had been expected); like vs as vs as if; as … as any; all the more.

topics.title: Articles and determiners at C1
topics.brief: Generic the (the tiger, the rich); zero article with abstract and institutional nouns (in hospital, at university); the with superlatives, ordinals and unique things; quite a / rather a / such a; half/all/both (of); a with jobs and units of measure; determiner + own.

topics.title: Word formation at C1
topics.brief: Nominalising suffixes (-ance/-ence/-ity/-ism/-hood); negative prefixes and their nuances (dis-/mis-/un-/in-/non-); compound adjectives (well-established, time-consuming); conversion (to google); -en/-ify/-ise verbs; strategy for Use of English Part 3.

topics.title: Phrasal verbs, dependent prepositions and idioms
topics.brief: Phrasal verbs with several meanings; what particles mean (up = completion, out = disappearance, off = separation, through = completion); separable/inseparable; dependent prepositions (Use of English Part 2); idiomatic collocations for C1 speaking and writing.
